clue.text: Bearing adversity, drink a sort of gin? That's cheating

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the drink and the jumbled spirit carry the trouble inside them

parts.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits

indicators.note: a sort of suggests a variant version, so the three letters of the spirit are rearranged

parts.note: a cross to bear is a trial or hardship

explanation.surface: Someone toughing out hard times with a stiff drink of some odd gin, which a stern observer calls cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' turns GIN into ING; DOUBLE plus ING then holds CROSS, the burden it is 'Bearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying someone you appear to support is treacherous, deceitful behaviour, i.e. cheating.

clue.text: One that's crossed over is not one suffering for deceit

indicators.note: suffering hints at the letters being knocked about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A turncoat is said not to be someone who pays a price for his treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not one' tells you to drop I from the pool; rearranging FOR and DECEIT without that I ('suffering') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who switches allegiance to the enemy side has literally crossed over to it.

clue.text: A foreign article getting no female sacked, as not publicised

parts.note: una is the Italian and Spanish for 'a', the indefinite article

indicators.note: no means without, so one letter is taken out of the word for dismissed

parts.note: sacked means fired from a job

explanation.surface: A piece in a foreign paper, written without any woman being dismissed, never made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never broadcast or aired has not been made public.

clue.text: Weapon used by police in Eilat, historically

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A note on what the officers in the Israeli resort of Eilat carried in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is the heavy bamboo baton carried by police in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The long iron-bound bamboo stick of South Asian police is a club-type weapon.

clue.text: See 1
Automatically approves Johnny's time when entertaining politician

parts.note: a johnny is British slang for a condom, also called a rubber; the 's gives the S

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: as can mean when (as he arrived = when he arrived)
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Johnny has a moment of hospitality, playing host to a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnny' is not a man's name here: in British slang a johnny is a condom, so it gives RUBBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To give official assent without real scrutiny is the idiom for passing something on the nod.

clue.text: Something fishy about someone making over 500 runs? Suspect something is afoot

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fish goes around the cricketer

parts.note: a smelt is a small fish
Brian Lara, the West Indies batsman, scored 501 not out in an English county match in 1994

explanation.surface: Doubts about a batsman's enormous score, as if something suspicious lay behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs are the points scored in cricket, and 501 not out is the highest first-class innings ever. 'about' puts the batsman inside the fish, straight after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense that some deception or trickery is going on.

clue.text: Keen to show decimal point

parts.note: a decimal system counts in tens
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone eager to demonstrate a decimal point on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decimal point' looks like one phrase; it splits into 'decimal' and 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and intense both describe strong, eager, concentrated feeling.

clue.text: Young girl's horse?

parts.note: the nursery word a small child, such as a little girl, would use for a horse

explanation.surface: A little girl's pony.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is British baby talk for a horse; the outside letters of 'young girl' are also G and G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is childish slang for a pony or any steed, so it is the word a young child uses.

clue.text: Model into safe sex, primarily out in gorges

indicators.note: into tells you the car's letter goes inside the rearranged letters
out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
primarily means first, so only the opening letter of sex is used

parts.note: the Model T was the classic Ford car

explanation.surface: Advice on bringing a fashion model round to the idea of safe sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SAFE plus S into FEASS, and T goes in to give the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat greedily; feasts used as a verb means the same.

clue.text: Peg's after a playwright? Not the one who's never arrived

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed from the dramatist's name

parts.note: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright
I is the Roman numeral one
a tee is a golf peg; 's after says it is placed last

explanation.surface: A golf peg follows a dramatist, who for once isn't the person who never shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: A then IBSEN without I gives ABSEN, and the peg follows. 'who's never arrived' stands as a noun phrase for the person missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present, who has failed to turn up at all, is missing from the roll.

clue.text: Victoria by train, arriving here? Yes and no

definitions.text: Victoria by train, arriving here? Yes and no

parts.words: Victoria by train, arriving here? Yes and no
parts.note: Victoria in London is the terminus for long-distance buses; you arrive there, yes, but not by train

explanation.surface: Arriving at London's Victoria by rail: is this the place?
explanation.walkthrough: London's Victoria has a railway station and, nearby, the main terminus for long-distance buses, so arriving at Victoria is right but arriving by train is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The bus terminus at Victoria is a real London destination reached by long-distance coach.

clue.text: No veggie creation ultimately, with Welshman in mind

indicators.note: in tells you the pieces go inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in look after

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of creation is used

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A vegetarian's take on Creation, with a Welshman considered at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-eater is the opposite of a vegetarian, so a flesh-eater is no veggie.

clue.text: What surgeon might use, cutting opening in unclothed heavenly body

indicators.note: in tells you the single letter goes inside the stripped word
unclothed means stripped, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a planet is a heavenly body

indicators.note: opening means the first letter

explanation.surface: A surgeon's tool cuts an opening into a bare celestial body.
explanation.walkthrough: PLANET 'unclothed' loses P and T to give LANE, and C goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a lancet, the sharp blade a doctor uses to open a boil.

clue.text: Those making maps of Scotland, for starters

definitions.text: Those making maps of Scotland, for starters

parts.words: Those making maps of Scotland, for starters
parts.note: the starters of 'of Scotland' are O and S, the initials of the British mapping agency

explanation.surface: The people who map Scotland, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The national mapping agency of Great Britain is known by its initials OS, which are the first letters of 'of Scotland'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British government agency charged with producing official national maps is a body of mapmakers.

clue.text: Less advanced slalom race arranged for anyone who wants to enter

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A beginners' slalom event set up as an open competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less' takes A from SLALOM RACE before the remaining letters are 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: An open event takes all challengers, so the phrase describes anybody who chooses to compete.

clue.text: You're certainly not this stupid!

parts.note: a remark to a solver: you are not stupid, and you are not short of clues either, since you are reading one

explanation.surface: A reassuring word to the solver that they are no fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer splits as 'clue-less': the reader is plainly not lacking a clue while reading one.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless is slang for foolish or dim, so it means stupid, while literally meaning lacking a clue.

clue.text: Ascetic lies about state of the Christian church

indicators.note: about means around, in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A self-denying holy man tells untruths about the condition of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like part of 'state of the Christian church'; it gives CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical is the formal adjective for things relating to the church or clergy.

clue.text: Nymph plays around when in company

indicators.note: when in says the jumbled letters sit inside the abbreviation
around suggests the letters spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: A nymph fools around when she is with other people.
explanation.walkthrough: Calypso is the sea nymph in Homer's Odyssey who kept Odysseus on her island.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a nymph of Greek myth, so the general word covers her as an example.

clue.text: Group of 50, in general

indicators.note: in tells you the numeral sits inside the general's name

parts.note: General Custer died at the Little Bighorn
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A body of fifty, considered broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' looks like the phrase 'generally'; it puts L inside CUSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster is a bunch or group of similar things gathered close together.

clue.text: In parliament, even Conservatives attack current leaders — it makes you sick

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the words that come before

explanation.surface: Tories in the Commons attacking the present leadership: enough to make you sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipecac is a root extract once used to make people vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecacuanha syrup was given as an emetic, a drug that induces vomiting.

clue.text: Disease shown by boil — operable, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A medical report: a boil that can be operated on, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'by' tells you the letters are found in 'boil — operable', in bOIL OPerable, and 'on reflection' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Poliomyelitis is a viral infection, a disease that once caused paralysis widely.

clue.text: Size of meal I'd put away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters sent off and put back in a different order

explanation.surface: How big was the meal I've eaten?
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' looks like the anagram signal and means eaten; 'put' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplitude means largeness or extent, so it is a word for size.

clue.text: Relative from one city in Merseyside area?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in tells you the city goes inside the region

parts.note: Merseyside, around Liverpool, is in the North West of England, NW
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A family member who comes from a city in the Liverpool area.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage, such as a mother of a spouse, is a relative.

clue.text: Prepare to print codicil, mostly with type having being reset

indicators.note: reset means set again in a new order, so the combined letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, here its first four letters

explanation.surface: Getting a codicil ready for printing after its type has been set again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' keeps four of the seven letters of CODICIL, giving CODI, a generous use of 'most'; CODI with TYPE is then 'having being reset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy-editing is checking and correcting a text before it goes to be printed.

clue.text: Happy and carefree as a Round the World sailor, say

indicators.note: say indicates that the word sounds like the name

parts.note: Sir Chay Blyth, the Scottish yachtsman, first sailed non-stop around the world westwards

explanation.surface: A cheerful description of a yachtsman circling the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: Chay Blyth is a famous British yachtsman, little known outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerfully unconcerned, a synonym of light-hearted.

clue.text: Wrong grid initially in puzzle — second in a row?

indicators.note: in tells you the pieces go inside the puzzle word

parts.note: a crossword is a puzzle
a wrong is a sin

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: A mistake in the grid makes this second puzzle in a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a row' looks like 'in succession'; it means quarrelling, while 'in' after 'initially' puts the pieces inside the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing swords is an idiom for arguing, so people doing so are having a row.
